-# Universal Cake Licensing Rationale
-10 Oct 2026 · @sirhc
-## Purpose and scope

-Universal Cake licenses its tools under AGPL-3.0-or-later and its content under Creative Commons, so that anything used to vet products and services stays open, inspectable and portable. This document records why, and weighs whether some content should move to Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike (CC BY-SA 4.0).

-It covers three kinds of work: the tools (code in `uc-radar` and related repositories), the radar evaluations (the Evaluation Metrics document and the placements on the assess, trial, adopt and re-review rings), and the wellbeing documentation. It is a rationale, not legal advice; the license texts themselves govern.
-## Current licensing at a glance
-Code is AGPL-3.0-or-later and content is Creative Commons, with one exception: the Evaluation Metrics document is currently AGPL-3.0-or-later too.
-| Work                        | Examples                                                     | Current license                       | Main reason                                                  |

-| Tools                       | `uc-radar`, `uc-cboard`, `universal-cake-themes`, build and scoring scripts | AGPL-3.0-or-later                     | Source stays available even when a tool runs as a hosted service |

-| Evaluation Metrics document | the versioned criteria for inclusive design, agency, environment, multilingual support, privacy, security, sovereignty and longevity | AGPL-3.0-or-later                     | Kept with the code that applies it                           |
-| Radar evaluations           | per-item write-ups, scores, ring placements                  | Creative Commons (variant to confirm) | Readers can reuse and cite findings freely                   |
-| Wellbeing documentation     | guides and procedures aimed at people rather than systems    | Creative Commons (variant to confirm) | Maximum reach, translation and adaptation                    |
-Open question: which Creative Commons variant is applied today, CC BY 4.0 or CC BY-SA 4.0? The rest of this document assumes CC BY 4.0 as the baseline.
-## Why AGPL-3.0-or-later for tools
-The AGPL is chosen because Universal Cake tools are likely to run as web services, and the AGPL is the GPL variant that keeps source available in that case (Free Software Foundation, 2007).
-- Network clause. Section 13 requires anyone who modifies the software and offers it to users over a network to give those users the corresponding source. A hosted radar cannot become a closed fork.
-- Agency and sovereignty. A client, NGO or municipality that adopts a tool can always obtain, audit, migrate and self-host it, which is the same test the radar applies to other products.
-- No lock-in by the practice itself. Vishpala cannot later close the tools on clients either; anyone holding a copy keeps the rights.
-- Consistency with the radar. A project that scores vendors on agency and longevity should pass its own criteria.
-- Or-later. The "or-later" clause lets the tools move to a future AGPL version without tracking down every contributor.
-The main cost is that some organizations have blanket policies against AGPL code. That friction is accepted for the tools, because hosted use is exactly the risk the license addresses.
-## Why Creative Commons for content

-Content uses Creative Commons rather than the AGPL because CC licenses are written for prose, images and data, while software licenses are written around source code and patents (Creative Commons, n.d.-a).

-- Fit. Creative Commons itself recommends against its licenses for software and in favour of FSF or OSI approved licenses, and supports CC for documentation (Creative Commons, n.d.-a). The reverse also holds: AGPL terms such as "corresponding source" map poorly onto a guide or an evaluation.
-- Recognition. Government bodies, NGOs and educators already know CC terms, so reuse rarely needs a legal review.

-- Version 4.0. The 4.0 licenses are international, cover sui generis database rights alongside copyright, and require reusers to indicate modifications (Creative Commons, n.d.-a). All three matter for evaluations and scored data.
-- No endorsement. Reusers may not imply that Universal Cake endorses their use or their version (Creative Commons, n.d.-a).
-- Trademarks are separate. CC licenses do not cover the Universal Cake name or marks, so the content can be open while the name stays a signal of origin (Creative Commons, n.d.-a).
-## Radar evaluations

-The radar's value is that its findings are traceable and reusable, so its license has to protect two things at once: free reuse of the findings, and clarity about which version is Universal Cake's own.

-- Facts are not owned. A score, a ring placement or a fact about a product is largely not copyrightable; the license reaches the written analysis, the criteria text and the selection and arrangement of the dataset. Any license choice therefore governs the reasoning more than the numbers.

-- Integrity through attribution, not restriction. The 4.0 duty to indicate modifications, plus the no-endorsement rule, means a third party can republish a modified evaluation but cannot present it as the original (Creative Commons, n.d.-a).
-- Versioning carries authority. Each evaluation names the metrics version it was scored against, so a fork scored under different criteria is visibly different.

-- The metrics document sits between code and content. It is AGPL today so that it travels with the scoring code. If it moves to CC BY-SA 4.0, it can still flow into the GPL family of tools through the one-way BY-SA to GPLv3 compatibility (Creative Commons, 2015), and GPLv3 section 13 allows combination with AGPL code.
-- Vendors as readers. Evaluated vendors may quote, rebut or republish an evaluation. A permissive or share-alike CC license allows that openly, which suits a project that wants scrutiny.
-## Wellbeing documentation

-Wellbeing documentation is the content most likely to be translated, printed, simplified and folded into someone else's materials, so its license should remove barriers for the organizations that serve aging and underserved people.
-- Adaptation is the point. Plain-language rewrites, large-print editions, offline copies and translations are all adaptations, and every CC license except the ND variants allows them.

-- Receiving organizations vary. Health networks, municipalities and NGOs often publish under their own terms, including CC BY, government open licences or all-rights-reserved. Their ability to absorb a page into a larger handbook decides whether the material reaches people.
-- Warranty disclaimer. CC licenses provide material as is (Creative Commons, n.d.-a). Wellbeing pages should still carry their own plain statement that they are not medical or professional advice.
-- Withdrawal is not possible. CC licenses cannot be revoked (Creative Commons, n.d.-a), so an outdated procedure stays in circulation. Version dates and a canonical URL are the practical fix.

-- Credit removal. An author who does not want to be associated with an adaptation can ask for the credit to be removed (Creative Commons, n.d.-a), which protects the practice from a harmful rewrite carrying its name.
-## CC BY-SA for some content: arguments for and against

-CC BY-SA 4.0 is the content counterpart of the AGPL's copyleft: anyone may adapt the work, but adaptations they share must stay under BY-SA or a designated compatible license (Creative Commons, n.d.-a). The question is where that guarantee is worth the friction it adds.
-### Arguments for
-- Improvements stay in the commons. A corrected evaluation or an improved translation cannot be taken private, which mirrors the reason for AGPL on the tools.
-- Philosophical consistency. Copyleft on both code and content tells clients the same story about agency and anti lock-in.

-- Bridge to the tools. CC BY-SA 4.0 is one-way compatible with GPLv3, so adaptations can be released under GPLv3 when content and code are hard to separate (Creative Commons, 2015). That suits the metrics document and any criteria text embedded in `uc-radar`.
-- Commons alignment. Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects use CC BY-SA, so radar findings or wellbeing material can flow into those articles without a license conflict.
-- Defence against enclosure. A consultancy or vendor cannot repackage the radar as a proprietary rating product with private improvements.
-### Arguments against

-- Friction for small governments and NGOs. Organizations that publish under their own licences, or all rights reserved, often cannot adapt BY-SA material into their own handbooks without relicensing the whole adaptation.
-- One-way flow. CC BY material can go into BY-SA works, but BY-SA material cannot go into CC BY works (Creative Commons, n.d.-a). Choosing BY-SA narrows who can build on the content.
-- Incompatible with NC. BY-SA adaptations cannot be combined with CC BY-NC material, which is common in education and health.
-- Limited reach over facts. Scores and placements are mostly uncopyrightable, so share-alike protects the prose more than the data people most want.
-- Collections escape it. Share-alike attaches to adaptations, not to placing an unmodified work beside other material, so a vendor can still quote or bundle an evaluation unchanged.
-- Compliance burden on reusers. Reusers must track license chains, which is a real cost for volunteers and translators.
-### By content type
-| Content                     | Case for BY-SA                                               | Case for BY                                                |
-| Evaluation Metrics document | Strong: keeps criteria forks open, bridges to GPL-family tools | Weak                                                       |
-| Radar evaluations           | Moderate: protects written analysis from private repackaging | Moderate: easier citation and quoting by vendors and press |
-| Wellbeing documentation     | Weak: share-alike blocks absorption into partner materials   | Strong: maximum reach to the people the work is for        |
-## Options and open questions
-The draft lean is a split: share-alike where forks are the risk, permissive where reach is the goal. This is provisional until the licensing owner confirms it.
-| Option                    | Metrics document           | Radar evaluations | Wellbeing documentation | Trade-off                                                   |
-| A. Split (draft lean)     | CC BY-SA 4.0, or keep AGPL | CC BY-SA 4.0      | CC BY 4.0               | Two content licenses to explain                             |
-| B. Share-alike everywhere | CC BY-SA 4.0               | CC BY-SA 4.0      | CC BY-SA 4.0            | Simplest copyleft story, least reach for wellbeing material |
-| C. Permissive everywhere  | CC BY 4.0                  | CC BY 4.0         | CC BY 4.0               | Widest reuse, no guard against private repackaging          |
-Open questions:
-- Which CC variant is on the content today?
-- Should the metrics document stay AGPL, move to CC BY-SA 4.0, or be dual licensed?
-- Is the scored dataset published separately from the prose, and does it need its own licence, for example CC0?
-- Does a trademark notice for the Universal Cake name need to sit beside each license statement?
-- Do any current or likely partners have policies that rule out BY-SA or AGPL?
-This document is a rationale, not legal advice; a lawyer familiar with Canadian copyright should review the final choice.
-## References
-Creative Commons. (2015, October 8). *CC BY-SA 4.0 now one-way compatible with GPLv3*. https://creativecommons.org/2015/10/08/cc-by-sa-4-0-now-one-way-compatible-with-gplv3/

-dc:creator: "Christopher Steel"
-dc:contributor: "Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), AI assistance"
-dc:subject: "SAT development process, repository standards, sync, release, test platforms"
-dc:description: "As-is record of how SAT development works across the radar, the automa, file-fairy, the OSAT managers and the product repositories, with findings for an improvement pass."
-dc:type: "Text"
-dc:format: "text/markdown"
-dc:identifier: "urn:uuid:cd696843-52b7-4406-a096-fc73df3bba05"

-# Overview: SAT Development, Current State
-Version: 0.1.0
-Status: Draft
-## Purpose and scope

-SAT development already runs on a coherent system: sat-doc-automa holds the canonical conventions and scripts, file-fairy distributes them, and product repositories receive them. The system is unevenly applied, and its procedures for new repositories, test platforms and releases are not yet written down in one place.

-This document records how things work today, as observed in the public repositories on 2026-10-07. It describes rather than prescribes. Findings are collected near the end as input for a separate improvement pass.

-In scope: sat-doc-automa, uc-radar, file-fairy, osat-manager-python and the other OSAT Fluent tools, sat, satx, and balise-sos-demo. Out of scope for now: client hosting, and websites not yet in a public repository.
-## The system at a glance
-Conventions and scripts move one way, from sat-doc-automa through file-fairy into each repository. Nothing carries product decisions back to the radar.
-```mermaid
-flowchart LR

- radar["uc-radar
Evaluates tools and approaches
Rings: adopt, assess, hold"]

- automa["sat-doc-automa
House rules and guides
Release ceremony scripts
One manifest per target"]

- osat["OSAT managers
User-space runtimes
manage-python 1.0"]

- fairy["file-fairy
plan, apply, status
Checksum drift record"]
-    subgraph targets["Receiving repositories"]
-        t1["uc-radar"]
-        t2["osat-manager-python"]
-        t3["file-fairy"]
-        t4["sat"]
-        t5["balise-sos-demo"]
-        t6["satx"]
-    end
-    radar -- adopts --> automa
-    automa -- manifests --> fairy
-    osat -- runtime --> fairy
-    fairy -- sync --> targets
-    targets -. "stack decisions in product ADRs do not return" .-> radar
-    classDef synced fill:#d8f0d8,stroke:#2e7d32,color:#000
-    classDef partial fill:#fff1cc,stroke:#b58100,color:#000
-    classDef none fill:#f8d7d7,stroke:#b3261e,color:#000
-    class t1,t2 synced
-    class t3,t4 partial
-    class t5,t6 none
-Key: green means synced with a state file recorded; amber means a manifest exists but no sync record was seen; red means no manifest in the automa.

-The radar decides what is adopted, the automa holds the canonical files, file-fairy distributes them on the runtimes the OSAT managers install, and the products receive them. Coverage is uneven: two targets show a sync record, two have a manifest but no record, and two have no manifest at all.
-## Resources
-Seven repositories carry the work, in three roles: governance (automa, radar), tooling (file-fairy, OSAT managers) and products (SAT, Balise).
-### sat-doc-automa, the canonical source
-sat-doc-automa [(Steel, 2026e)](#ref-steel-2026e) is the canonical home for style guides, formats, templates and automa across SAT, OSAT Fluent and Universal Cake. It holds:

-- Automa under `en/docs/automa/`, per format, with `defaults/` for rules in force and `examples/` for chosen alternatives: markdown rules, AI collaboration, licence blocks, and the shared CLAUDE.md signpost block.

-- Guides: five style guides (versioned documents, technical register, plain language, navigation and accessibility, APA 7) and the devops guides (Commit and Versioning Workflow v0-3-0, file-fairy Usage v0-1-0).
-- Decision records under `en/docs/decisions/devops/`, including gh CLI for release asset publishing.
-- The release ceremony scripts at the root: `bump-version.py`, `cut-release.py`, `publish-release.py`, `check-conformance.py`, `test_publish_release.py`, plus `normalize-metadata.py`.
-- Eleven file-fairy manifests, `ff-manifest-<target>.yaml`, one per receiving repository.
-It is deliberately structured as a SAT archive from its first commit, so it can become the first SAT archive with little rework.
-### uc-radar, the decision gate

-uc-radar [(Steel, 2026g)](#ref-steel-2026g) holds Universal Cake radar entries and the evaluation metrics. Entries sit under `en/docs/radar/` in rings `adopt/`, `assess/` and `hold/`, grouped by domain. Process documents live beside them: an evaluation lifecycle (v0-1-0), an entry template (v0-2-0) and a praxis evaluation prompt (v0-1-1). Metrics versions v0-3-1, v0-4-0-draft, v0-5-0-draft and v0-5-1 are all present. The current release is 0.2.4 (2026-09-29). It has received the shared zone from sat-doc-automa through file-fairy since 0.1.2 [(Steel, 2026h)](#ref-steel-2026h).
-### file-fairy, the distribution mechanism

-file-fairy [(Steel, 2026b)](#ref-steel-2026b) is a manifest-driven CLI with `plan`, `apply` and `status` verbs. It copies named groups of files from a source repository to a target on local disk and tracks drift by checksum in a per-target `.file-fairy-state.yaml`. Sync modes are `mirror` (the default), `seed_if_missing`, `overwrite` and `reference_only`. It also supports retraction (`state: absent`) and managed blocks inside files the target otherwise owns. It started as a radar entry, and it needs Python 3.8+ and PyYAML.
-### OSAT managers, the runtimes

-osat-manager-python [(Steel, 2026c)](#ref-steel-2026c), run as `manage-python`, installs self-contained CPython runtimes into user space without elevated privilege, a package manager or a compiler. It is at 1.0.x, verified end to end on Linux x86-64; the Windows aliases, `install.ps1` and macOS are not yet verified. It is the first of the OSAT collection to move from `-tool` installer to `-manager`. Siblings with manifests in the automa include the hugo, myrepos, rclone, restic, sat and wekan tools.
-### sat, the current SAT line

-sat [(Steel, 2026d)](#ref-steel-2026d) is Source Archive Tools: filesystem-first archive management with small standalone commands. Its README status reads `sat_version: 0.7.0`. It carries the content pipeline (metadata ingress, egress, transmog to MkDocs), `satlib`, and docs under `en/`. Tools live under `en/bin` and `en/lib`. Its README changelog records the tag drift of 0.4.1 to 0.4.3 that the current release workflow was written to prevent.
-### satx, SAT in development

-satx [(Steel, 2026f)](#ref-steel-2026f) is the development line. It already shows the newer design: a `.satx.assets` sidecar at the root, language-neutral `bin/` and `lib/`, language trees `en/`, `es/` and `fr/`, `venvs/.venvs.assets`, and a `satx-seed.tar.gz`. Its README is empty.
-### balise-sos-demo, the first product site

-balise-sos-demo [(Steel, 2026a)](#ref-steel-2026a) is the offline-first emergency procedures demonstration and the entry point of the Resilience Pack. It is an Eleventy build producing three copies from one build: installed web, a downloadable zip of about 170 KiB, and print. It is bilingual (`en/docs`, `fr-ca/docs`) with six ADRs, operator and editor guides, and a session log. It publishes with `npm run deploy:local` to an Incus web container on flow, without GitHub Actions (ADR-006). Its house rules under `en/docs/automa/` are described as synced from sat-doc-automa.
-## The shared repository kit
-A de facto standard repository already exists: the same root files recur across most repositories, delivered by file-fairy from sat-doc-automa.
-| File or path | Role | Delivered how |
-| `VERSION` | Single source of the version | Seeded once, then owned by the repo (`seed_if_missing` is the documented example) |
-| `CHANGELOG.md` | Repository changelog, Keep a Changelog format | Per repo |
-| `ROADMAP.md` | Forward plan | Per repo |
-| `CLAUDE.md` | AI collaboration signpost | Shared signpost block from `automa/claude-md/` |
-| `LICENSE` | Licence text | Per repo; licence blocks from `automa/licenses/` |
-| `bump-version.py` | Computes and writes the next version | Synced from automa, devops-scripts group |
-| `cut-release.py` | Bump, roll changelog, surgical commit, tag, stop before push | Synced from automa |
-| `publish-release.py` | Tarball, `SHA256SUMS`, optional GPG, via `gh` or a plain directory | Synced from automa |
-| `check-conformance.py` | Lints markdown against house rules | Synced from automa |
-| `test_publish_release.py` | Offline tests for the publish ceremony | Synced from automa |

-## Procedures as practised

-Only the release ceremony and the sync are written down. New repository and test platform setup are reconstructed here from what the repositories contain, and steps marked (inferred) need confirming.
-### New repository
-1. Create the repository on GitHub under steelcj and clone it locally (inferred).
-2. Write a manifest `ff-manifest-<repo>.yaml` in sat-doc-automa naming the groups the repo receives.
-3. Run `file-fairy plan`, then `file-fairy apply`, against the manifest.
-4. Commit what arrived as its own commit, the receive-then-commit pattern in the file-fairy Usage guide; uc-radar records this as a changelog entry.
-5. Add the repo's own `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `ROADMAP.md` and `en/docs/` content (inferred).
-### Keeping a repository current
-1. Change the canonical file in sat-doc-automa.
-2. Run `file-fairy plan` per manifest to see `new`, `update` and `conflict` items.
-3. Run `apply`; conflicts on `mirror` items are skipped unless `--force` is given.
-4. Commit the received files in each target.
-There is no single command that runs every manifest, so propagation depends on remembering which targets exist (inferred).
-### Release
-From the Commit and Versioning Workflow v0-3-0, the ceremony in four steps:
-1. Write the changelog entries under `[Unreleased]`.
-2. Run `cut-release.py`: bump, roll the changelog, surgical commit, tag, stop before push.
-3. Push the commit and the tag.
-4. Run `publish-release.py`: deterministic tarball, `SHA256SUMS`, optional GPG signature, published with `gh` or to a plain directory.
-sat predates the synced kit and uses its own `bump-sat-version.py`.
-### Test platforms
-Three kinds are in use, each set up per project:
-- Unit and offline tests in the repo root, run with `python3 test_*.py` (file-fairy, osat-manager-python, and the publish ceremony everywhere).
-- End-to-end runs on Linux, such as `e2e_manage_python.py`, presumably inside Incus containers on flow (inferred).
-- Windows 11 VM validation through `validate-windows.ps1` in osat-manager-python.
-Balise adds `npm run check`: an offline link check and markdown conformance.
-### Publishing a site

-Balise builds with `npm run build` into `_site/` and deploys with `npm run deploy:local` to an Incus web container on flow.local. ADR-006 records the choice of self-hosted publishing without GitHub Actions. sat's README shows the older path: `archive-init.py` creating a MkDocs docs tree for chrissteel.com.

-## Findings for the improvement pass
-The largest gap is that decisions are made in product repositories and do not flow back to the radar. The rest are coverage and drift issues that the existing tooling can already fix.
-| Area | Finding | Evidence |
-| Radar and practice | Tools in daily use are still in `assess` | Incus is in `assess/containers` but hosts Balise and the test platforms; Caddy is in `assess/webservers` despite scoring very high |
-| Radar and practice | Product ADRs decide stack choices outside the radar | Balise ADR-001 (Eleventy) and ADR-006 (self-hosted publishing) have no matching radar entries seen |
-| Radar and practice | Three radar locations | uc-radar; file-fairy cites `sat-doc-automa/en/docs/radar/assess/sync/`; sat links `en/docs/radar/ROADMAP.md` |
-| Sync coverage | Not every repo is on a manifest | No manifest for balise-sos-demo, satx, or osat-manager-python under its new name |
-| Sync coverage | Manifests exist that seem unapplied | `ff-manifest-sat` and `ff-manifest-file-fairy` exist, yet neither target shows a state file or, for sat, the kit scripts |
-| Sync coverage | No way to run all manifests at once | Propagation is one `plan` and `apply` per manifest |
-| Naming | The `-tool` to `-manager` rename is unfinished | Manifests still named `osat-fluent-*-tool`; osat-fluent-restic-tool referenced by file-fairy |
-| Paths | Docs roots and guide paths differ | `en/docs/` versus `docs/en/` (restic tool); `en/docs/devops/` versus `en/docs/guides/devops/`; sat uses `en/bin` while satx has root `bin/` |

-| Licensing | Licence choice is inconsistent and partly undocumented | Balise GPL-3.0, sat AGPL-3.0, uc-radar and file-fairy with no LICENSE file; the automa README lists GPL and CC BY blocks while file-fairy references an AGPL block not listed |

-| Versioning | Filename versions depart from the spec | The spec is `-vX.Y.Z` before 1.0.0 and no version from 1.0.0; uc-radar 0.2.3 renamed about seventy files to `-vX-Y-Z` on an AI assumption, and later work copied the pattern; uc-radar's `versioning-postfix-rules-v0-1-0.md`, added in the same release, should be checked |
-| Versioning | Several versions of one document coexist with no current marker | Metrics v0-3-1, v0-4-0-draft, v0-5-0-draft and v0-5-1 side by side |
-| Versioning | README status and changelogs drift from releases | sat README says 0.7.0, its changelog stops at 0.5.0; file-fairy says 0.1.0 Draft while describing post-0.2.0 features |
-| Changelog quality | Entries are not curated | uc-radar 0.2.3 is a pasted `git status`; 0.1.2 and 0.2.0 repeat one entry |
-| Bootstrap | A fresh machine has no written path | file-fairy install hard-codes `/home/initial/.local/bin/python3.12`; the order manage-python, then file-fairy, then sync is implied, not stated |
-| Test platforms | Each project builds its own | Linux e2e scripts, a Windows VM script and npm checks, with no shared definition of a test container or VM |
-| Publishing | A Vishpala-wide stance lives in one product | Self-hosting without GitHub Actions is Balise ADR-006, not an automa decision |
-| Process records | Good models exist but are not part of the kit | Balise has a session log and role guides; satx has an empty README |
-| Small defects | Typos and stale links | file-fairy licence line reads "file-faiexiexry"; sat README links the install guide twice, once without a version suffix |

+## Purpose and scope

+SAT development already runs on a coherent system: sat-doc-automa holds the canonical conventions and scripts, file-fairy distributes them, and product repositories receive them. The system is unevenly applied, and its procedures for new repositories, test platforms and releases are not yet written down in one place.

+This document records how things work today, as observed in the public repositories on 2026-10-07. It describes rather than prescribes. Findings are collected near the end as input for a separate improvement pass.

+In scope: sat-doc-automa, uc-radar, file-fairy, osat-manager-python and the other OSAT Fluent tools, sat, satx, and balise-sos-demo. Out of scope for now: client hosting, and websites not yet in a public repository.

+The full record is the uc-automa session record, `en-ca/docs/sessions/2026-10-21--osat-manager-git-and-the-manager-pattern-v0.1.0.md` (https://github.com/steelcj/uc-automa). This note is the short version, to start the next chat from.
+## Decided
+- **conda-forge git on Linux, macOS and Windows.** uc-radar *Git on Windows* 0.2.0: conda-forge git in Trial, MinGit in Assess as the fallback, dugite-native in Hold.

+- **The package's system gitconfig is kept.** manage-git writes its own per-version file that includes the package's and sets the baseline, read through `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`. Other managers start git from the `invocation` that `--check --json` reports (osat-manager-git 0001).
+- **Baseline 1 and conventions** (osat-manager-git 0002, open as PR #2):
+  - git 2.49.0 or later and `core.autocrlf = false`; on Windows also `core.longpaths = true` and Git Credential Manager; no `safe.directory`;
+  - `manager.yaml` uses `arch` and `verification.signature`;
+  - locks ship with the manager at `locks/<version>/<subdir>.json`;
+  - Windows gets a real `git.exe` through a `current` junction;
+  - uninstall leaves nothing behind and writes no registry;
+  - gettext message catalogues come later, through osat-manager-core.
+- **uc-automa 0033:** managers run on manage-python's manager runtime, never on a version they expose.
+- **uc-automa 0034:** option C for mise. OSAT managers stay per-tool and standard-library on client machines; mise is the reference and an approved release-time tool for locks.
+- **uc-automa 0035:** the shared package is osat-manager-core, in its own repository, installed once into the manager runtime.
+- **uc-automa 0036:** a check exits 0 when ready, 2 when not ready, 1 when it could not run.
+- **Process guide** *Creating an OSAT Manager Repository* is at 0.6.0.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
#
# source
#   project: sat-doc-automa
#   path: publish-release.py
#
"""
publish-release.py, publish a cut release: build a byte-stable tarball
for an already-pushed tag, compute SHA256SUMS, optionally GPG-sign the
checksum file, and publish the artifacts through a provider backend.
This script owns the publishing ceremony only. Cutting stays in
cut-release.py (bump, changelog roll, commit, tag), and pushing stays a
human act over whatever transport the maintainer trusts; this script
runs strictly after both, per
decision--publish-release-shared-script-with-provider-interface.
Connectivity is two layers. Transport (git push, tags) is provider
agnostic and this script uses it only for preflight, `git ls-remote` to
confirm the tag is on the remote. The publish channel (creating the
release, attaching assets) is provider specific and is reached through
a small backend seam:
    detect(remote_url)   which provider is this repository on
    preflight()          is the channel ready for this tag
    publish(tag, files)  create the release, attach the artifacts
    release_url(tag)     where consumers will find them
The seam obeys gold--interfaces-stay-honest-to-the-narrowest-backend:
a release IS files at stable locations plus SHA256SUMS plus an optional
signature, because that is all the narrowest backend (a plain
directory) can express. Anything richer a provider offers is carried
inside that provider's backend or not at all.
Backends: `gh` (GitHub, auto-detected from the origin URL) and `dir`
(a local directory, the narrowest backend, selected explicitly with
--backend dir --target DIR; also the offline test fixture).
Usage:
    publish-release.py                    publish VERSION's tag via the
                                          detected backend
    publish-release.py --dry-run          everything except publish
    publish-release.py --backend dir --target DIR
    publish-release.py --no-sign          skip GPG even if available
    publish-release.py --sign             require GPG, fail if absent
Sequence: guard (tag exists locally, tag:VERSION matches) -> transport
preflight (tag on remote via ls-remote) -> backend detect and preflight
-> build tarball twice from `git archive` and refuse on any byte
difference (the determinism gate, checked on every run, not assumed)
-> SHA256SUMS -> optional GPG detached signature -> publish -> report
the release URL.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
#
# source
#   project: uc-cboard
#   path: build-release.py
#
"""
build-release.py, cut a uc-cboard release from a pinned upstream cboard tag.
This is a maintainer-run script, never an end-user tool. It has no
relationship to manage-cboard.py (the osat-fluent-cboard-tool consumer),
which only ever fetches what this script publishes.
Sequence:
    1. Resolve the target upstream tag (cboard-org/cboard) to a commit SHA
    2. Shallow-clone that commit into a scratch directory
    3. yarn install --ignore-scripts   (verified 2026-08-06: completes clean)
    4. yarn build, with REDACTED
       (default heap OOMs on this build; confirmed via V8 heap-exhaustion
       trace, not a code failure — see scoping notes)
    5. Package build/ as a tarball
    6. Write a SHA256 checksum
    7. Report the artefact path and checksum; publishing the GitHub
       Release itself is a separate, deliberate step (not automated here,
       matching cut-release.py's stance of stopping before push)
Usage:
    build-release.py --tag 1.39.0
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path
UPSTREAM_REPO = "cboard-org/cboard"
UPSTREAM_CLONE_URL = f"https://github.com/{UPSTREAM_REPO}.git"
API_TAG_URL = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{UPSTREAM_REPO}/git/refs/tags"
SCRATCH_DIR = Path("scratch-cboard")
DIST_DIR = Path("dist")
BUILD_ENV_EXTRA = {"NODE_OPTIONS": "--max-old-space-size=4096"}
def fail(msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"[BUILD ERROR] {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)
def run(cmd: list[str], cwd: Path, env: dict | None = None) -> None:
    full_env = os.environ.copy()
    if env:
        full_env.update(env)
    result = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=cwd, env=full_env)
    if result.returncode != 0:
        fail(f"command failed ({result.returncode}): {' '.join(cmd)}")
def resolve_tag_sha(tag: str) -> str:
    url = f"{API_TAG_URL}/{tag}"
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "uc-cboard-build"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
            data = json.loads(resp.read())
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
        fail(f"could not resolve tag {tag!r} via GitHub API: {exc}")
    sha = data.get("object", {}).get("sha")
    if not sha:
        fail(f"unexpected API response resolving tag {tag!r}: {data!r}")
    return sha

def build() -> None:
    run(["yarn", "install", "--ignore-scripts"], cwd=SCRATCH_DIR)
    run(["yarn", "build"], cwd=SCRATCH_DIR, env=BUILD_ENV_EXTRA)
    if not (SCRATCH_DIR / "build" / "index.html").is_file():

def package(tag: str, sha: str) -> Path:
    DIST_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    artefact_name = f"uc-cboard-{tag}.tar.gz"
    artefact_path = DIST_DIR / artefact_name
    build_dir = SCRATCH_DIR / "build"

    with tarfile.open(artefact_path, "w:gz") as tar:
        tar.add(build_dir, arcname=f"cboard-{tag}")

    checksum = hashlib.sha256(artefact_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    checksum_path = DIST_DIR / f"{artefact_name}.sha256"
    checksum_path.write_text(f"{checksum}  {artefact_name}\n", encoding="utf-8")

    provenance_path = DIST_DIR / f"uc-cboard-{tag}.provenance.json"
    provenance_path.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "upstream_repo": UPSTREAM_REPO,
                "upstream_tag": tag,
                "upstream_commit": sha,
                "artefact": artefact_name,
                "sha256": checksum,
            },
            indent=2,
        )
        + "\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    return artefact_path


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Cut a uc-cboard release.")

    sha = resolve_tag_sha(args.tag)

    print("[BUILD] cloning at pinned commit...")
    clone_at_commit(sha)

    print("[BUILD] installing (--ignore-scripts) and building...")
    build()

    print("[BUILD] packaging artefact...")
    artefact_path = package(args.tag, sha)

uc-cboard still isn't published. The third build installed everything with Node 22.14.0, but it ran out of memory during `yarn build`. The kernel's out-of-memory killer stopped Node at about 4.2 GB, the 4 GB heap limit the build is set to plus overhead.

The machine has 15.3 GB of RAM, but only about 5 GB is free. The 2 GB swap is completely full, and other apps hold the rest: Jan's local model worker, Brave, LibreOffice and others.

Three ways forward:

1. **Free some memory, then I retry (my recommendation).** Closing Jan (or unloading its model), LibreOffice and some Brave tabs should be enough. The build settings stay the same as for the 0.1.2 release.
2. **Build without source maps** (`GENERATE_SOURCEMAP=false`). This uses much less memory, but the published bundle would have no `.map` files, unlike the build that 0.1.2 was made from.
3. **Add swap.** That needs `sudo`, so you'd run it yourself, for example `! sudo fallocate -l 8G /swapfile2 && sudo chmod 600 /swapfile2 && sudo mkswap /swapfile2 && sudo swapon /swapfile2`.

Let me know which you'd like. Everything else is ready: dependencies are installed, so a retry goes straight to `yarn build`. The `build-release.py` fix (07e80bc) is committed locally but not pushed.

- This machine's system Node 18 can't build current Cboard; it needs Node 20 or later. I didn't change the build script to choose a Node version.
- Upstream Cboard has reached 1.42.x, if you want to move the pin in a later release.

# Decision: An eleventy-site Layout

Version: 0.1.0
Status: Accepted

## Context

eleventy-website-vishpala-com, the repository for vishpala.com, is the first Vishpala repository that is a website rather than a Python tool. It holds an Eleventy configuration, an npm manifest and lockfile, the site's input under `src/`, and a theme under `themes/`. The root is always closed and a path no layout describes is a finding about the layout, with no per-repository exception (uc-automa 0013), so under `base` alone every one of those paths is a finding.

Eleventy fixes some names by default. It looks for its configuration as `eleventy.config.js`; inside its input directory it reads data from `_data/` and layouts and partials from `_includes/`; and it reads directory and template data from files named for their folder or template with `.11tydata.json` or `.11tydata.js`, such as `guides.11tydata.json`. The directive `naming/lowercase-names` already exempts names a tool requires, such as `REUSE.toml`, but its check listed only `REUSE.toml`, so it reported every one of these.

## Decision

- Add the layout `eleventy-site`, extending `base` directly, since a website is not a Python tool.
- It requires `eleventy.config.js`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `src/`, and allows `themes/`. These are what an Eleventy site holds when set up as Eleventy and npm expect by default, so a site conforms without configuring anything away from those defaults.
- It also allows `netlify.toml`, for a site deployed to Netlify. Netlify reads its configuration from that file at the root of the repository, so the build settings, redirects and response headers can be kept and reviewed with the site rather than only in Netlify's dashboard.
- `src/` and `themes/` stay open: their contents are the site's own and change with it, and the layout does not describe them.
- The built output and installed dependencies, such as `_site/` and `node_modules/`, are not described. They are ignored by `.gitignore`, so the layout check never sees them.
- The check for `naming/lowercase-names` accepts the names Eleventy requires: `eleventy.config.js` everywhere; and, in a repository whose layout chain includes `eleventy-site`, the directories `_data/` and `_includes/` and the `.11tydata.json` and `.11tydata.js` suffixes under `src/`. The part of a data file's name before the suffix still follows the rule, so `Guides.11tydata.json` and `a.b.11tydata.json` are still reported. The directive's text already covers names a tool requires, so this is a check fixed without changing the rule (uc-automa 0029), and the directive keeps its version.

## Alternatives considered

**A general `website` layout.** Rejected for now. What a site holds at the top level depends on its generator, and only one generator is in use. A shared parent can be drawn out of `eleventy-site` when a second generator arrives.

**Generating Netlify's `_headers` and `_redirects` into the built site instead of allowing `netlify.toml`.** Not chosen as the only way. Those files carry redirects and headers but not the build command or the publish directory, which would then live only in Netlify's dashboard. A site can still generate them alongside `netlify.toml`, since they are output and never committed.

**Describing the configuration files of other hosts as well.** Not done yet. Only Netlify is in use; another host's file joins the layout when a site deploys there.

**Requiring the Sveltia CMS files.** Rejected. Where the CMS's `admin/` lives depends on the site's input directory, and a site can be built without a CMS.

**Configuring Eleventy away from its defaults, such as with `.eleventy.js`.** Rejected. A site should work out of the box as Eleventy documents it, and the layout follows the site rather than the reverse.

## Consequences

- `uc-automa init --layout eleventy-site` writes the same subscriptions as `base`, since the layout adds no `from_offering` paths.
- The seeded `REUSE.toml` covers a Python tool's usual paths, so each site adds annotations for `src/`, `themes/`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` and `eleventy.config.js`, and for any font licences, as its own record.
- The directory guide gains a section for the layout.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.1.0 | 2026-10-23 | Accepted | Initial version |

"""uc-automa docs index: the generated documentation index (uc-automa 0009).

{language}/docs/README.md lists every document under {language}/docs/,
section by section, with its title, version and status from its front
matter. It is generated, marked as generated, and never edited by hand.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional

import yaml

from . import frontmatter

GENERATED = ("<!-- Generated by uc-automa docs index from each document's "
             "front matter; do not edit by hand. -->")
SECTIONS = [("directives", "Directives"), ("guides", "Guides"),
            ("decisions", "Decisions"), ("references", "References"),
            ("sessions", "Sessions")]


class IndexError_(Exception):
    """The index cannot be generated."""


def sidecar_defaults(root: Path) -> dict:
    """Dublin Core defaults from the repository's SAT sidecar."""
    config = root / ".uc-automa.yaml"
    if not config.is_file():
        raise IndexError_(".uc-automa.yaml not found")
    with config.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        repository = (yaml.safe_load(f) or {}).get("repository")
    dc = root / f".{repository}.assets" / "dc.yaml"
    if not dc.is_file():
        raise IndexError_(f"{dc.relative_to(root).as_posix()} not found; "
                          f"the index takes its creator and rights from it")
    with dc.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f) or {}


def escape(text: str) -> str:
    return str(text).replace("|", "\\|")


def render_index(root: Path, language: str,
                 files: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> str:
    defaults = sidecar_defaults(root)
    creator = defaults.get("dc:creator")
    rights = defaults.get("dc:rights")
    if not creator or not rights:
        raise IndexError_("the sidecar's dc.yaml needs dc:creator and "
                          "dc:rights")
    docs = f"{language}/docs/"
    if files is None:
        files = sorted(p.relative_to(root).as_posix()
                       for p in (root / docs).rglob("*.md"))
    lines = [GENERATED, "", "# Documentation", "",
             f"Every document under `{docs}`, with its version and status, "
             f"taken from its front matter.", ""]
    for directory, heading in SECTIONS:
        prefix = docs + directory + "/"
        rows = []
        for rel in sorted(f for f in files
                          if f.startswith(prefix) and f.endswith(".md")):
            try:
                data, _ = frontmatter.read(root.joinpath(*rel.split("/")))
            except (ValueError, yaml.YAMLError) as exc:
                raise IndexError_(f"{rel}: {exc}") from None
            data = data or {}
            title = escape(data.get("title", rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]))
            link = rel[len(docs):]
            rows.append(f"| [{title}]({link}) | "
                        f"{escape(data.get('sat:version', ''))} | "
                        f"{escape(data.get('sat:status', ''))} |")
        if rows:
            lines += [f"## {heading}", "", "| Document | Version | Status |",
                      "| --- | --- | --- |", *rows, ""]
    licence = LICENCE_NAMES.get(rights, rights)
    lines += ["## License", "",
              f"This index, generated by uc-automa from the documents it "
              f"lists, by **{creator}**, is licensed under {licence}.", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


LICENCE_NAMES = {
    "CC-BY-SA-4.0": "the [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 "
                    "International License](https://creativecommons.org/"
                    "licenses/by-sa/4.0/)",

class UcAutoma(unittest.TestCase):
    """The acceptance checks on uc-automa itself."""

    def test_check_passes_on_uc_automa(self):
        code, out, err = run("check", "--target", str(support.REPO))
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out + err)

    def test_offerings_plan_has_nothing_to_do(self):
        code, out, err = run("offerings", "plan", "--target",
                             str(support.REPO))
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, err)
        self.assertIn("0 item(s) would be synced", out)
        self.assertIn("0 conflict(s)", out)

    def test_translations_report_nothing_for_en_ca(self):
        code, out, err = run("translations", "--target", str(support.REPO))
        self.assertEqual(code, 0, out + err)
        self.assertIn("0 error(s)", out)
        self.assertNotIn("stale:", out)

    def test_index_is_generated_from_front_matter(self):
        shutil.copytree(support.FIXTURES / "docs" / "generated-index" /
                        "fail" / "index-missing", self.root,
                        dirs_exist_ok=True)
        code, out, err = run("docs", "index", "--target", str(self.root))
        # The fixture pins 0.1.0; on another version the pin check refuses.
        if code == 0:
            text = (self.root / "en-ca/docs/README.md").read_text()
            self.assertTrue(text.startswith("<!-- Generated by uc-automa"))
            self.assertIn("[Using](guides/usage/using-v0.1.0.md)", text)
        else:
            self.assertIn("pins uc-automa", err)


class Metadata(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_new_id_is_a_random_urn_uuid(self):
        import uuid
        code, out, _ = run("metadata", "new-id")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        value = out.strip()
        self.assertTrue(value.startswith("urn:uuid:"), value)
        self.assertEqual(uuid.UUID(value[len("urn:uuid:"):]).version, 4)

    def test_each_id_is_new(self):
        first, second = run("metadata", "new-id")[1], run("metadata", "new-id")[1]
        self.assertNotEqual(first, second)

"""The extends rules (uc-automa 0013), one test per rule."""

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import support  # noqa: F401

from uc_automa.conformance.layouts import load_layout
from uc_automa.errors import AutomaError

BASE = """format: 1
describes: "base"
source_language: "en-ca"
placeholders:
  language: '^[a-z]{2}(-[a-z]{2})?$'
tree:
  - path: "README.md"
    type: file
    required: false
  - path: "docs/"
    type: directory
    closed: true
    children:
      - path: "index.md"
        type: file
"""


class Extends(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.conf = Path(self._tmp.name)
        (self.conf / "layouts").mkdir()
        self.write("base", BASE)

    def tearDown(self):
        self._tmp.cleanup()

    def write(self, name, text):
        (self.conf / "layouts" / f"{name}.yaml").write_text(text)

    def child(self, tree, extra=""):
        self.write("child", 'format: 1\ndescribes: "child"\nextends: "base"\n'
                   'source_language: "en-ca"\n' + extra + "tree:\n" + tree)
        return load_layout(self.conf, "child")

    def refused(self, tree, extra="", says=""):
        with self.assertRaises(AutomaError) as caught:
            self.child(tree, extra)
        self.assertIn(says, str(caught.exception))


class RealLayouts(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_every_layout_resolves(self):
        for name in ("base", "python-tool", "uc-automa", "osat-manager",
                     "eleventy-site"):
            with self.subTest(layout=name):
                load_layout(support.REPO / "conf", name)

    def test_the_chain_is_base_python_tool_then_the_type(self):
        for name in ("uc-automa", "osat-manager"):
            layout = load_layout(support.REPO / "conf", name)
            self.assertEqual(layout.chain, ["base", "python-tool", name])

    def test_eleventy_site_extends_base_directly(self):
        layout = load_layout(support.REPO / "conf", "eleventy-site")
        self.assertEqual(layout.chain, ["base", "eleventy-site"])

    def test_eleventy_site_allows_netlify_toml(self):
        layout = load_layout(support.REPO / "conf", "eleventy-site")

class Node:
    name: str                       # this segment, such as "docs/"
    path: str                       # the full pattern, such as "{language}/docs/"
    type: str
    added_by: str                   # the layout that introduced the path
    required: object = False
    kind: Optional[str] = None
    generated: bool = False
    closed: bool = False
    from_offering: Optional[str] = None
    parent: Optional["Node"] = None
    children: List["Node"] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def top(self) -> "Node":
        node = self
        while node.parent is not None:
            node = node.parent
        return node

    @property
    def effective_kind(self) -> Optional[str]:
        return self.top.kind

    @property
    def is_literal(self) -> bool:
        return "{" not in self.name


@dataclass
class Layout:
    id: str
    chain: List[str]                         # base first
    format: int
    source_language: str
    placeholders: Dict[str, str]
    tree: List[Node]
    own_paths: Dict[str, Set[str]]           # layout id -> paths it added
    own_placeholders: Dict[str, Set[str]]    # layout id -> placeholders

    def nodes(self) -> List[Node]:
        out: List[Node] = []

        def walk(nodes):
            for node in nodes:
                out.append(node)
                walk(node.children)
        walk(self.tree)
        return out

-# Overview: SAT Development, Current State
-Version: 0.1.0
-Status: Draft
-## Purpose and scope

-SAT development already runs on a coherent system: sat-doc-automa holds the canonical conventions and scripts, file-fairy distributes them, and product repositories receive them. The system is unevenly applied, and its procedures for new repositories, test platforms and releases are not yet written down in one place.

-This document records how things work today, as observed in the public repositories on 2026-10-07. It describes rather than prescribes. Findings are collected near the end as input for a separate improvement pass.

-In scope: sat-doc-automa, uc-radar, file-fairy, osat-manager-python and the other OSAT Fluent tools, sat, satx, and balise-sos-demo. Out of scope for now: client hosting, and websites not yet in a public repository.
-## The system at a glance
-Conventions and scripts move one way, from sat-doc-automa through file-fairy into each repository. Nothing carries product decisions back to the radar.
-```mermaid
-flowchart LR

- radar["uc-radar
Evaluates tools and approaches
Rings: adopt, assess, hold"]

- automa["sat-doc-automa
House rules and guides
Release ceremony scripts
One manifest per target"]

- osat["OSAT managers
User-space runtimes
manage-python 1.0"]

- fairy["file-fairy
plan, apply, status
Checksum drift record"]
-    subgraph targets["Receiving repositories"]
-        t1["uc-radar"]
-        t2["osat-manager-python"]
-        t3["file-fairy"]
-        t4["sat"]
-        t5["balise-sos-demo"]
-        t6["satx"]
-    end
-    radar -- adopts --> automa
-    automa -- manifests --> fairy
-    osat -- runtime --> fairy
-    fairy -- sync --> targets
-    targets -. "stack decisions in product ADRs do not return" .-> radar

-Key: green means synced with a state file recorded; amber means a manifest exists but no sync record was seen; red means no manifest in the automa.

-The radar decides what is adopted, the automa holds the canonical files, file-fairy distributes them on the runtimes the OSAT managers install, and the products receive them. Coverage is uneven: two targets show a sync record, two have a manifest but no record, and two have no manifest at all.
-## Resources
-Seven repositories carry the work, in three roles: governance (automa, radar), tooling (file-fairy, OSAT managers) and products (SAT, Balise).
-### sat-doc-automa, the canonical source
-sat-doc-automa [(Steel, 2026e)](#ref-steel-2026e) is the canonical home for style guides, formats, templates and automa across SAT, OSAT Fluent and Universal Cake. It holds:

-- Automa under `en/docs/automa/`, per format, with `defaults/` for rules in force and `examples/` for chosen alternatives: markdown rules, AI collaboration, licence blocks, and the shared CLAUDE.md signpost block.

-- Guides: five style guides (versioned documents, technical register, plain language, navigation and accessibility, APA 7) and the devops guides (Commit and Versioning Workflow v0-3-0, file-fairy Usage v0-1-0).
-- Decision records under `en/docs/decisions/devops/`, including gh CLI for release asset publishing.
-- The release ceremony scripts at the root: `bump-version.py`, `cut-release.py`, `publish-release.py`, `check-conformance.py`, `test_publish_release.py`, plus `normalize-metadata.py`.
-- Eleven file-fairy manifests, `ff-manifest-<target>.yaml`, one per receiving repository.
-It is deliberately structured as a SAT archive from its first commit, so it can become the first SAT archive with little rework.
-### uc-radar, the decision gate

-uc-radar [(Steel, 2026g)](#ref-steel-2026g) holds Universal Cake radar entries and the evaluation metrics. Entries sit under `en/docs/radar/` in rings `adopt/`, `assess/` and `hold/`, grouped by domain. Process documents live beside them: an evaluation lifecycle (v0-1-0), an entry template (v0-2-0) and a praxis evaluation prompt (v0-1-1). Metrics versions v0-3-1, v0-4-0-draft, v0-5-0-draft and v0-5-1 are all present. The current release is 0.2.4 (2026-09-29). It has received the shared zone from sat-doc-automa through file-fairy since 0.1.2 [(Steel, 2026h)](#ref-steel-2026h).
-### file-fairy, the distribution mechanism

-file-fairy [(Steel, 2026b)](#ref-steel-2026b) is a manifest-driven CLI with `plan`, `apply` and `status` verbs. It copies named groups of files from a source repository to a target on local disk and tracks drift by checksum in a per-target `.file-fairy-state.yaml`. Sync modes are `mirror` (the default), `seed_if_missing`, `overwrite` and `reference_only`. It also supports retraction (`state: absent`) and managed blocks inside files the target otherwise owns. It started as a radar entry, and it needs Python 3.8+ and PyYAML.
-### OSAT managers, the runtimes

-osat-manager-python [(Steel, 2026c)](#ref-steel-2026c), run as `manage-python`, installs self-contained CPython runtimes into user space without elevated privilege, a package manager or a compiler. It is at 1.0.x, verified end to end on Linux x86-64; the Windows aliases, `install.ps1` and macOS are not yet verified. It is the first of the OSAT collection to move from `-tool` installer to `-manager`. Siblings with manifests in the automa include the hugo, myrepos, rclone, restic, sat and wekan tools.
-### sat, the current SAT line

-sat [(Steel, 2026d)](#ref-steel-2026d) is Source Archive Tools: filesystem-first archive management with small standalone commands. Its README status reads `sat_version: 0.7.0`. It carries the content pipeline (metadata ingress, egress, transmog to MkDocs), `satlib`, and docs under `en/`. Tools live under `en/bin` and `en/lib`. Its README changelog records the tag drift of 0.4.1 to 0.4.3 that the current release workflow was written to prevent.
-### satx, SAT in development

-satx [(Steel, 2026f)](#ref-steel-2026f) is the development line. It already shows the newer design: a `.satx.assets` sidecar at the root, language-neutral `bin/` and `lib/`, language trees `en/`, `es/` and `fr/`, `venvs/.venvs.assets`, and a `satx-seed.tar.gz`. Its README is empty.
-### balise-sos-demo, the first product site

-balise-sos-demo [(Steel, 2026a)](#ref-steel-2026a) is the offline-first emergency procedures demonstration and the entry point of the Resilience Pack. It is an Eleventy build producing three copies from one build: installed web, a downloadable zip of about 170 KiB, and print. It is bilingual (`en/docs`, `fr-ca/docs`) with six ADRs, operator and editor guides, and a session log. It publishes with `npm run deploy:local` to an Incus web container on flow, without GitHub Actions (ADR-006). Its house rules under `en/docs/automa/` are described as synced from sat-doc-automa.
-## The shared repository kit
-A de facto standard repository already exists: the same root files recur across most repositories, delivered by file-fairy from sat-doc-automa.
-| File or path | Role | Delivered how |
-| `VERSION` | Single source of the version | Seeded once, then owned by the repo (`seed_if_missing` is the documented example) |
-| `CHANGELOG.md` | Repository changelog, Keep a Changelog format | Per repo |
-| `ROADMAP.md` | Forward plan | Per repo |
-| `CLAUDE.md` | AI collaboration signpost | Shared signpost block from `automa/claude-md/` |
-| `LICENSE` | Licence text | Per repo; licence blocks from `automa/licenses/` |
-| `bump-version.py` | Computes and writes the next version | Synced from automa, devops-scripts group |
-| `cut-release.py` | Bump, roll changelog, surgical commit, tag, stop before push | Synced from automa |
-| `publish-release.py` | Tarball, `SHA256SUMS`, optional GPG, via `gh` or a plain directory | Synced from automa |
-| `check-conformance.py` | Lints markdown against house rules | Synced from automa |
-| `test_publish_release.py` | Offline tests for the publish ceremony | Synced from automa |
-| `normalize-metadata.py` | Metadata normalisation | Present in automa, uc-radar, osat-manager-python; not listed in the automa README |
-| `.file-fairy-state.yaml` | Record of the last sync | Written by file-fairy in the target |
-| `en/docs/` | Language-rooted documentation | Convention, plus synced devops guides and automa |

-Per-document conventions ride on top: Dublin Core and `sat:` front matter, versioned filenames (the spec is `-vX.Y.Z` before 1.0.0 and no version in the filename from 1.0.0; most repositories currently use `-vX-Y-Z`), a changelog table in each document, and a License section built from the licence blocks.
-## Procedures as practised

-Only the release ceremony and the sync are written down. New repository and test platform setup are reconstructed here from what the repositories contain, and steps marked (inferred) need confirming.
-### New repository
-1. Create the repository on GitHub under steelcj and clone it locally (inferred).
-2. Write a manifest `ff-manifest-<repo>.yaml` in sat-doc-automa naming the groups the repo receives.
-3. Run `file-fairy plan`, then `file-fairy apply`, against the manifest.
-4. Commit what arrived as its own commit, the receive-then-commit pattern in the file-fairy Usage guide; uc-radar records this as a changelog entry.
-5. Add the repo's own `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `ROADMAP.md` and `en/docs/` content (inferred).
-### Keeping a repository current
-1. Change the canonical file in sat-doc-automa.
-2. Run `file-fairy plan` per manifest to see `new`, `update` and `conflict` items.
-3. Run `apply`; conflicts on `mirror` items are skipped unless `--force` is given.
-4. Commit the received files in each target.
-There is no single command that runs every manifest, so propagation depends on remembering which targets exist (inferred).
-### Release
-From the Commit and Versioning Workflow v0-3-0, the ceremony in four steps:
-1. Write the changelog entries under `[Unreleased]`.
-2. Run `cut-release.py`: bump, roll the changelog, surgical commit, tag, stop before push.
-3. Push the commit and the tag.
-4. Run `publish-release.py`: deterministic tarball, `SHA256SUMS`, optional GPG signature, published with `gh` or to a plain directory.
-sat predates the synced kit and uses its own `bump-sat-version.py`.
-### Test platforms
-Three kinds are in use, each set up per project:
-- Unit and offline tests in the repo root, run with `python3 test_*.py` (file-fairy, osat-manager-python, and the publish ceremony everywhere).
-- End-to-end runs on Linux, such as `e2e_manage_python.py`, presumably inside Incus containers on flow (inferred).
-- Windows 11 VM validation through `validate-windows.ps1` in osat-manager-python.
-Balise adds `npm run check`: an offline link check and markdown conformance.
-### Publishing a site

-Balise builds with `npm run build` into `_site/` and deploys with `npm run deploy:local` to an Incus web container on flow.local. ADR-006 records the choice of self-hosted publishing without GitHub Actions. sat's README shows the older path: `archive-init.py` creating a MkDocs docs tree for chrissteel.com.

-## Findings for the improvement pass
-The largest gap is that decisions are made in product repositories and do not flow back to the radar. The rest are coverage and drift issues that the existing tooling can already fix.
-| Area | Finding | Evidence |
-| Radar and practice | Tools in daily use are still in `assess` | Incus is in `assess/containers` but hosts Balise and the test platforms; Caddy is in `assess/webservers` despite scoring very high |
-| Radar and practice | Product ADRs decide stack choices outside the radar | Balise ADR-001 (Eleventy) and ADR-006 (self-hosted publishing) have no matching radar entries seen |
-| Radar and practice | Three radar locations | uc-radar; file-fairy cites `sat-doc-automa/en/docs/radar/assess/sync/`; sat links `en/docs/radar/ROADMAP.md` |
-| Sync coverage | Not every repo is on a manifest | No manifest for balise-sos-demo, satx, or osat-manager-python under its new name |
-| Sync coverage | Manifests exist that seem unapplied | `ff-manifest-sat` and `ff-manifest-file-fairy` exist, yet neither target shows a state file or, for sat, the kit scripts |
-| Sync coverage | No way to run all manifests at once | Propagation is one `plan` and `apply` per manifest |
-| Naming | The `-tool` to `-manager` rename is unfinished | Manifests still named `osat-fluent-*-tool`; osat-fluent-restic-tool referenced by file-fairy |
-| Paths | Docs roots and guide paths differ | `en/docs/` versus `docs/en/` (restic tool); `en/docs/devops/` versus `en/docs/guides/devops/`; sat uses `en/bin` while satx has root `bin/` |

-| Licensing | Licence choice is inconsistent and partly undocumented | Balise GPL-3.0, sat AGPL-3.0, uc-radar and file-fairy with no LICENSE file; the automa README lists GPL and CC BY blocks while file-fairy references an AGPL block not listed |

-| Versioning | Filename versions depart from the spec | The spec is `-vX.Y.Z` before 1.0.0 and no version from 1.0.0; uc-radar 0.2.3 renamed about seventy files to `-vX-Y-Z` on an AI assumption, and later work copied the pattern; uc-radar's `versioning-postfix-rules-v0-1-0.md`, added in the same release, should be checked |
-| Versioning | Several versions of one document coexist with no current marker | Metrics v0-3-1, v0-4-0-draft, v0-5-0-draft and v0-5-1 side by side |
-| Versioning | README status and changelogs drift from releases | sat README says 0.7.0, its changelog stops at 0.5.0; file-fairy says 0.1.0 Draft while describing post-0.2.0 features |
-| Changelog quality | Entries are not curated | uc-radar 0.2.3 is a pasted `git status`; 0.1.2 and 0.2.0 repeat one entry |
-| Bootstrap | A fresh machine has no written path | file-fairy install hard-codes `/home/initial/.local/bin/python3.12`; the order manage-python, then file-fairy, then sync is implied, not stated |
-| Test platforms | Each project builds its own | Linux e2e scripts, a Windows VM script and npm checks, with no shared definition of a test container or VM |
-| Publishing | A Vishpala-wide stance lives in one product | Self-hosting without GitHub Actions is Balise ADR-006, not an automa decision |
-| Process records | Good models exist but are not part of the kit | Balise has a session log and role guides; satx has an empty README |
-| Small defects | Typos and stale links | file-fairy licence line reads "file-faiexiexry"; sat README links the install guide twice, once without a version suffix |

-# osat-manager-git: where things stand after 2026-10-21

-The full record is the uc-automa session record, `en-ca/docs/sessions/2026-10-21--osat-manager-git-and-the-manager-pattern-v0.1.0.md` (https://github.com/steelcj/uc-automa). This note is the short version, to start the next chat from.
-## Decided
-- **conda-forge git on Linux, macOS and Windows.** uc-radar *Git on Windows* 0.2.0: conda-forge git in Trial, MinGit in Assess as the fallback, dugite-native in Hold.

-- **The package's system gitconfig is kept.** manage-git writes its own per-version file that includes the package's and sets the baseline, read through `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`. Other managers start git from the `invocation` that `--check --json` reports (osat-manager-git 0001).
-- **Baseline 1 and conventions** (osat-manager-git 0002, open as PR #2):
-  - git 2.49.0 or later and `core.autocrlf = false`; on Windows also `core.longpaths = true` and Git Credential Manager; no `safe.directory`;
-  - `manager.yaml` uses `arch` and `verification.signature`;
-  - locks ship with the manager at `locks/<version>/<subdir>.json`;
-  - Windows gets a real `git.exe` through a `current` junction;
-  - uninstall leaves nothing behind and writes no registry;
-  - gettext message catalogues come later, through osat-manager-core.
-- **uc-automa 0033:** managers run on manage-python's manager runtime, never on a version they expose.
-- **uc-automa 0034:** option C for mise. OSAT managers stay per-tool and standard-library on client machines; mise is the reference and an approved release-time tool for locks.
-- **uc-automa 0035:** the shared package is osat-manager-core, in its own repository, installed once into the manager runtime.
-- **uc-automa 0036:** a check exits 0 when ready, 2 when not ready, 1 when it could not run.
-- **Process guide** *Creating an OSAT Manager Repository* is at 0.6.0.
-- **No `sat:migration_status`.** satx *Ingress Verification Stamp* v0.0.1, under consideration, has SAT mark content verified at ingress, with the SAT version that ingressed it.

"""uc-automa docs index: the generated documentation index (uc-automa 0009).

{language}/docs/README.md lists every document under {language}/docs/,
section by section, with its title, version and status from its front
matter. It is generated, marked as generated, and never edited by hand.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import List, Optional

import yaml

from . import frontmatter

GENERATED = ("<!-- Generated by uc-automa docs index from each document's "
             "front matter; do not edit by hand. -->")
SECTIONS = [("directives", "Directives"), ("guides", "Guides"),
            ("decisions", "Decisions"), ("references", "References"),
            ("sessions", "Sessions")]


class IndexError_(Exception):
    """The index cannot be generated."""


def sidecar_defaults(root: Path) -> dict:
    """Dublin Core defaults from the repository's SAT sidecar."""
    config = root / ".uc-automa.yaml"
    if not config.is_file():
        raise IndexError_(".uc-automa.yaml not found")
    with config.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        repository = (yaml.safe_load(f) or {}).get("repository")
    dc = root / f".{repository}.assets" / "dc.yaml"
    if not dc.is_file():
        raise IndexError_(f"{dc.relative_to(root).as_posix()} not found; "
                          f"the index takes its creator and rights from it")
    with dc.open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f) or {}


def escape(text: str) -> str:
    return str(text).replace("|", "\\|")


def render_index(root: Path, language: str,
                 files: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> str:
    defaults = sidecar_defaults(root)
    creator = defaults.get("dc:creator")
    rights = defaults.get("dc:rights")
    if not creator or not rights:
        raise IndexError_("the sidecar's dc.yaml needs dc:creator and "
                          "dc:rights")
    docs = f"{language}/docs/"
    if files is None:
        files = sorted(p.relative_to(root).as_posix()
                       for p in (root / docs).rglob("*.md"))
    lines = [GENERATED, "", "# Documentation", "",
             f"Every document under `{docs}`, with its version and status, "
             f"taken from its front matter.", ""]
    for directory, heading in SECTIONS:
        prefix = docs + directory + "/"
        rows = []
        for rel in sorted(f for f in files
                          if f.startswith(prefix) and f.endswith(".md")):
            try:
                data, _ = frontmatter.read(root.joinpath(*rel.split("/")))
            except (ValueError, yaml.YAMLError) as exc:
                raise IndexError_(f"{rel}: {exc}") from None
            data = data or {}
            title = escape(data.get("title", rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]))
            link = rel[len(docs):]
            rows.append(f"| [{title}]({link}) | "
                        f"{escape(data.get('sat:version', ''))} | "
                        f"{escape(data.get('sat:status', ''))} |")
        if rows:
            lines += [f"## {heading}", "", "| Document | Version | Status |",
                      "| --- | --- | --- |", *rows, ""]
    licence = LICENCE_NAMES.get(rights, rights)
    lines += ["## License", "",
              f"This index, generated by uc-automa from the documents it "
              f"lists, by **{creator}**, is licensed under {licence}.", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


LICENCE_NAMES = {
    "CC-BY-SA-4.0": "the [Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 "
                    "International License](https://creativecommons.org/"
                    "licenses/by-sa/4.0/)",
    "CC-BY-4.0": "the [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International "
                 "License](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)",
}


def write_index(root: Path, language: str) -> Path:
    path = root / language / "docs" / "README.md"
    text = render_index(root, language)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as f:
        f.write(text)
    return path

"""The extends rules (uc-automa 0013), one test per rule."""

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

import support  # noqa: F401

from uc_automa.conformance.layouts import load_layout
from uc_automa.errors import AutomaError

BASE = """format: 1
describes: "base"
source_language: "en-ca"
placeholders:
  language: '^[a-z]{2}(-[a-z]{2})?$'
tree:
  - path: "README.md"
    type: file
    required: false
  - path: "docs/"
    type: directory
    closed: true
    children:
      - path: "index.md"
        type: file
"""


class Extends(unittest.TestCase):

    def setUp(self):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.conf = Path(self._tmp.name)
        (self.conf / "layouts").mkdir()
        self.write("base", BASE)

    def tearDown(self):
        self._tmp.cleanup()

    def write(self, name, text):
        (self.conf / "layouts" / f"{name}.yaml").write_text(text)

    def child(self, tree, extra=""):
        self.write("child", 'format: 1\ndescribes: "child"\nextends: "base"\n'
                   'source_language: "en-ca"\n' + extra + "tree:\n" + tree)
        return load_layout(self.conf, "child")

    def refused(self, tree, extra="", says=""):
        with self.assertRaises(AutomaError) as caught:
            self.child(tree, extra)
        self.assertIn(says, str(caught.exception))

    def test_a_chain_resolves_parent_first(self):
        layout = self.child('  - path: "notes/"\n    type: directory\n')
        self.assertEqual(layout.chain, ["base", "child"])
        self.assertEqual(layout.own_paths["child"], {"notes/"})

    def test_a_cycle_is_an_error(self):
        self.write("base", BASE.replace('describes: "base"',
                                        'describes: "base"\nextends: "child"'))
        self.refused('  - path: "x"\n    type: file\n', says="cycle")

    def test_required_may_tighten(self):
        layout = self.child('  - path: "README.md"\n    type: file\n'
                            '    required: true\n')
        self.assertIs(layout.tree[0].required, True)

    def test_required_may_never_loosen(self):
        self.write("base", BASE.replace("required: false", "required: true"))
        self.refused('  - path: "README.md"\n    type: file\n'
                     '    required: false\n', says="never loosen")

    def test_type_may_not_change(self):
        self.refused('  - path: "docs"\n    type: file\n', says="type")

    def test_kind_may_be_set_where_none_is(self):
        layout = self.child('  - path: "README.md"\n    type: file\n'
                            '    kind: meta\n')
        self.assertEqual(layout.tree[0].kind, "meta")

    def test_kind_may_not_change(self):
        self.write("base", BASE.replace('    required: false\n',
                                        '    required: false\n    kind: read\n', 1))
        self.refused('  - path: "README.md"\n    type: file\n    kind: meta\n',
                     says="may not change kind")

    def test_kind_only_on_top_level_nodes(self):
        self.refused('  - path: "docs/"\n    type: directory\n    children:\n'
                     '      - path: "extra.md"\n        type: file\n'
                     '        kind: read\n', says="top-level")

    def test_descendants_inherit_kind(self):
        layout = self.child('  - path: "docs/"\n    type: directory\n'
                            '    kind: read\n    children:\n'
                            '      - path: "extra.md"\n        type: file\n')
        extra = [n for n in layout.nodes() if n.path == "docs/extra.md"][0]
        self.assertEqual(extra.effective_kind, "read")

    def test_from_offering_may_be_set_but_not_changed(self):
        layout = self.child('  - path: "README.md"\n    type: file\n'
                            '    from_offering: "readme"\n')
        self.assertEqual(layout.tree[0].from_offering, "readme")
        self.write("base", BASE.replace('    required: false\n',
                                        '    required: false\n'
                                        '    from_offering: "one"\n', 1))
        self.refused('  - path: "README.md"\n    type: file\n'
                     '    from_offering: "two"\n', says="from_offering")

    def test_closed_may_close_but_never_reopen(self):
        layout = self.child('  - path: "notes/"\n    type: directory\n')
        self.assertFalse(layout.tree[-1].closed)
        self.refused('  - path: "docs/"\n    type: directory\n'
                     '    closed: false\n', says="reopen")

    def test_paths_added_inside_a_closed_directory_count_as_declared(self):
        layout = self.child('  - path: "docs/"\n    type: directory\n'
                            '    children:\n      - path: "extra.md"\n'
                            '        type: file\n')
        self.assertIn("docs/extra.md", layout.own_paths["child"])

    def test_inherited_placeholders_may_not_be_redefined(self):
        self.refused('  - path: "x"\n    type: file\n',
                     extra="placeholders:\n  language: '^x$'\n",
                     says="redefines")

    def test_source_language_only_under_the_language_placeholder(self):
        self.refused('  - path: "x"\n    type: file\n'
                     '    required: source-language\n', says="source-language")

    def test_format_and_source_language_match_the_chain(self):
        self.write("child", 'format: 1\ndescribes: "child"\nextends: "base"\n'
                   'source_language: "fr-ca"\ntree: []\n')
        with self.assertRaises(AutomaError):
            load_layout(self.conf, "child")

    def test_undefined_placeholders_are_refused(self):
        self.refused('  - path: "{nothing}.md"\n    type: file\n',
                     says="undefined")


class RealLayouts(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_every_layout_resolves(self):
        for name in ("base", "python-tool", "uc-automa", "osat-manager",
                     "eleventy-site"):
            with self.subTest(layout=name):
                load_layout(support.REPO / "conf", name)

    def test_the_chain_is_base_python_tool_then_the_type(self):
        for name in ("uc-automa", "osat-manager"):
            layout = load_layout(support.REPO / "conf", name)
            self.assertEqual(layout.chain, ["base", "python-tool", name])

    def test_eleventy_site_extends_base_directly(self):
        layout = load_layout(support.REPO / "conf", "eleventy-site")
        self.assertEqual(layout.chain, ["base", "eleventy-site"])

    def test_eleventy_site_allows_netlify_toml(self):
        layout = load_layout(support.REPO / "conf", "eleventy-site")
        self.assertIn("netlify.toml", layout.own_paths["eleventy-site"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
